name: Misborn
body:
Even psychopomps can make mistakes. Sometimes a soul waiting in Purgatory goes slightly astray at just the wrong time in just the wrong place. Sometimes a yamaraj that has spent too long away from Purgatory shows enough favoritism to give a soul a “second chance,” even though this would result in their speedy destruction if ever discovered. And sometimes, a psychopomp’s indiscretion goes even further than that.

The misborn are the human descendants of psychopomps or reincarnated humanoid souls that spent long periods of time in Purgatory. They are a type of planetouched, though one that is exceptionally—and perhaps thankfully—rare. When they are found, they are often treated as psychics or mediums. It is uncommon that a misborn’s true heritage is plain knowledge.

Physical Description: Misborn’s appearances vary sharply, but they are invariably tall and spindly, looming like herons above the rest of their families.They generally stand at least six feet tall, and have been known to grow as high as eight. Common features for misborn include white or sunken eyes, extremely desaturated skin and hair colors, unnatural marks on their skin (such as mask-like patterns), sooty feathers mixed in with their hair, abnormally long fingers, thin lips, and the smells of herbs, carrion, or embalming fluid.

Society: As misborn are rarely properly identified they are seldom shunned for their heritage, but some communities avoid them strictly for their supernatural abilities or strange appearances alone. Misborn tend to either be extremely social or extreme hermits—those descended from catrinas in particular surround themselves with people, witnessing lives and deaths with a fascination not even they fully understand. Misborn are too uncommon to form their own societies, but they always feel an unexplained kinship on the rare occasion they encounter others of their kind.

Relations: Most misborn wrongly identify as humans (as they are born from human parents), and others treat them as such. They find themselves more at home among outcasts such as half-elves and half-orcs, but they almost always retain a sense of being out-of-place. Due to their taciturn natures, dwarves have the easiest time interacting with misborn, and some misborn find pleasant employ looking after dwarven tombs.

Alignment and Religion: Misborn, even the more social ones, tend not to associate themselves with movements or causes of any sort, and are almost always Neutral. They naturally feel close connections to gods of death.

Adventurers: Adventure represents an opportunity to avoid large crowds and be close to death: two pastimes that appeal to many misborn. Misborn especially like the sort of dungeon delving that involves old tombs.

Core Traits (14 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: Misborn possess an abnormally strong connection to their surroundings, and move with spiderlike speed and grace despite their gangliness, but their connection to life has always been somewhat weak. They gain +2 Wisdom, +2 Dexterity, and –2 Constitution.
Type: Misborn are outsiders with the native subtype. 3 RP
Size: Misborn are Medium creatures and receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Speed: Misborn have a base speed of 30 feet.
Languages: Misborn begin play speaking Common. Misborn with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Abyssal, Celestial, Dwarven, Elven, Halfling, Infernal, and Orc.
Other Traits
Undead Fighter: Guided by a subconscious loathing, misborn gain a +1 racial bonus on attack rolls against undead. Lifesense does not detect misborn. 2 RP
Darkvision: Misborn can see perfectly in the dark for up to 60 feet.
Ghostly Link: Misborn retain a certain connection to the Ethereal Plane. Misborn can see ethereal creatures as though using see invisibility. 2 RP
Soul Seer: Misborn have the uncanny ability to detect death in the world around them. They gain the following spell-like ability: 4 RP
Constant—deathwatch
Spiritspeech: Misborn can speak with dead at will, though the corpse may automatically resist the spell if it chooses. The target is under no compulsion to answer accurately or at all. There is no limit to the number of questions a misborn can ask, and this usage does not prevent castings of speak with dead within the week. 5 RP
Death Vulnerability: Misborn take a –2 penalty on saves against death effects. –2 RP
Alternate Racial Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of existing misborn traits.

One Foot in the Grave: Some misborn are related to people who died and were returned to life a few too many times. A misborn with this trait can, as an immediate action, flawlessly feign death. It does not breathe in this state, and its heart does not beat, nor can it move or act in any way save to exit the state as a full-round action. To all examinations, it appears to be absolutely dead. Its hit points are unchanged, and it can still take damage while in this state. After exiting this state, it is exhausted for 1 hour. Misborn who take this trait gain vulnerability to negative energy damage, taking 50% more damage from such attacks, and they take a -4 penalty on Constitution checks made to stabilize.
Petitioner’s Shackles: Some misborn are very closely related to a soul who spent a long time in Purgatory rather than a psychopomp. Once per day, using a token such as dice or a spirit board, the misborn may attempt to contact their ancestor to ask a single question and receive a brief answer. This otherwise functions as augury with an effectiveness of 80%. This trait replaces spiritspeech.
Skin and Bones: Some misborn are exceptionally thin, even by their kind’s standards. These misborn gain DR 1/bludgeoning, but gain vulnerability to cold.
Undead Guide: Some misborn have the power to hypnotize the unliving. Once per day as a full-round action, a misborn can create a 20-foot-radius burst that causes undead creatures within the aura’s range to become fascinated for one minute (as the bard’s fascinate bardic performance). Affected undead may resist this effect by making a successful Will saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 the misborn HD + Charisma modifier). Mindless undead can never consider themselves threatened unless they are actively attacked while fascinated. This is a necromancy effect similar to command undead, and not a mind-affecting effect. This trait replaces undead fighter.
